interpretations: Towns are those of the customer who placed the order. Only towns with at least one invoice line item appear. Per-item averages use only non-null values. The ratio is derived_product_cost / derived_total_cost per line, and rows with a zero or null denominator are ignored or excluded. The cross-town average is the plain average of the town-level average ratios, so each town counts equally. Towns with a ratio above this are shown with town, average price, average ratio, and the excess over the cross-town average
The cross-town average is the average of the ratio over all invoice line items, so each line counts equally and towns with more lines weigh more. Towns above it are shown, with the same columns
The cross-town average is the average of the per-(order item, town) averaged ratios across all groups, so each group counts equally. Towns above it are shown, with the same columns
The town's average price is the average of the per-order-item average prices, and each order item counts equally within a town. Alternatively, it is the average over all of the town's lines

Grouping is by order_item_id and town only, so the same order item id can appear in only one town. Alternatively, grouping uses `Invoice_Line_Items.order_item_id` as given, even where it disagrees with `Order_Items.order_id` or the order reached through the invoice

The ratio is computed per line before averaging, so it is the average of the line ratios. Alternatively, it is the ratio of the summed costs, or the ratio of the average cost to the average total cost
"Above" means strictly greater than the cross-town average, so towns equal to it are excluded. Alternatively, "above or equal" is meant
"Excess" is the town's average ratio minus the cross-town average, which is a signed difference and is always positive here. Alternatively, it is a percentage or relative excess
Towns with a null or missing town value are excluded. Alternatively, they are treated as one group and included
Integer division is possible if the cost columns were integers. Here they are decimals, so the ratio is a real number. Results are returned unrounded
Towns with the same name in different states or countries are merged into one town. Alternatively, they are kept as separate towns by town, state and country
Invoice line items whose invoice has no order, or whose order has no customer, are dropped by the inner joins. Alternatively, they are kept with a null town
Results are in no particular order. Alternatively, they are ordered by excess descending or by town name
Not all interpretations are covered. These are missing:
The per-item average price and average ratio are each computed over their own non-null rows, rather than only over rows where both the price and the ratio are non-null
Town names that differ only by letter case or surrounding whitespace are treated as the same town, rather than as distinct towns
Towns whose average ratio is null (every line had a null or zero denominator) are left out of the cross-town average, rather than counted as zero
queries:
WITH t AS (
  SELECT c.town_city AS town,
         AVG(ili.product_price) AS avg_price,
         AVG(CASE WHEN ili.derived_total_cost IS NOT NULL
                   AND ili.derived_total_cost <> 0
                   AND ili.derived_product_cost IS NOT NULL
                  THEN ili.derived_product_cost * 1.0 / ili.derived_total_cost
             END) AS avg_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Invoices i ON ili.invoice_number = i.invoice_number
  JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY c.town_city
)
SELECT town,
       avg_price,
       avg_ratio,
       avg_ratio - (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM t) AS excess
FROM t
WHERE avg_ratio > (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM t);
SELECT c.town_city, AVG(ili.derived_vat_payable * 1.0 / ili.derived_product_cost) AS avg_ratio
FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
JOIN Invoices i ON ili.invoice_number = i.invoice_number
JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY c.town_city
HAVING AVG(ili.derived_vat_payable * 1.0 / ili.derived_product_cost) > (
  SELECT AVG(derived_vat_payable * 1.0 / derived_product_cost)
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items
);
WITH g AS (
  SELECT ili.order_item_id, c.town_city,
         AVG(ili.derived_total_cost * 1.0 / ili.derived_product_cost) AS avg_ratio
  FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
  JOIN Invoices i ON ili.invoice_number = i.invoice_number
  JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
  JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
  GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city
)
SELECT order_item_id, town_city, avg_ratio
FROM g
WHERE avg_ratio > (SELECT AVG(avg_ratio) FROM g);
SELECT c.town_city, AVG(ili.product_price) AS average_price
FROM Customers c
JOIN Orders o ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN Invoices i ON i.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN Invoice_Line_Items ili ON ili.invoice_number = i.invoice_number
GROUP BY c.town_city;
SELECT ili.order_item_id, c.town_city
FROM Invoice_Line_Items ili
JOIN Invoices i ON ili.invoice_number = i.invoice_number
JOIN Orders o ON i.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN Customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
GROUP BY ili.order_item_id, c.town_city;
SELECT AVG(derived_product_cost * 1.0 / derived_total_cost) FROM Invoice_Line_Items;
